data.name: Tabitha
data.long_meaning: In Aramaic, Tabitha means 'gazing at God' or 'rejoicing in God'. In the New Testament, Tabitha is a disciple and a widow whom Peter brought back to life.

in_hebrew.name: טביתא
in_hebrew.meaning: טביתא - צביון של שימחה וטוב לב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: טביתא הוא שם עברי שמקורו בברית החדשה של הברית הישנה, שם נקראת אישה צעירה שפטר לוקסוס ועל ידי השליח פטרוס. המשמעות היא 'צביון של שימחה וטוב לב', והיא מוזכרת בברית החדשה, מעשי השליחים 9:36-41, כאישה יעילה ובעלת לב טוב.

in_greek.name: Ταβίθα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ταβίθα είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος που προέρχεται από την αραμαϊκή λέξη 'Ταβיתא', που σημαίνει 'Ζωστήρια' ή 'αναζωπύρωσις'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, συγκεκριμένα στις Πράξεις των Αποστόλων 9:36-41, αναφέρεται μια χήρα γυναίκα, μαθήτρια του Κυρίου, με το όνομα Ταβίθα, που έκανε καλές πράξεις και βοήθησε τους φτωχούς.

in_latin.name: Tabitha
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Tabitha in Latina scriptura similiter ut in Graeca, refert ad nomen hebraicum quod significat 'gazella' vel 'velox'. In Ecclesia primitiva, Tabitha fuit mulier christiana quae Actibus Apostolorum 9:36-41 commemoratur, quae operibus bonis et eleemosynis suis in vita christiana excelluit.

in_english.name: Tabitha
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tabitha originates from the Hebrew word 'Tavitha,' meaning 'gazelle' or 'swift.' It is also associated with goodness and kindness. In the New Testament, Acts 9:36-41, Tabitha is a Christian woman known for her charitable works and kindness, particularly in helping the poor. The name symbolizes swiftness, gentleness, and piety. Historically, Tabitha has been used across various Christian cultures, signifying a person of compassion and generosity.

biblical_reference.note: Tabitha, also known as Dorcas, was a follower of Christ mentioned in the New Testament.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tabitha has a rich cultural history in Christianity. It represents a devoted follower of Christ who demonstrated her faith through acts of kindness and generosity. Tabitha was known for her charitable works and was described as a "woman full of good works and acts of mercy" (Acts 9:36). Her name and her story continue to inspire Christians today, reminding us of the importance of compassion, love, and selflessness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tabitha is a powerful reminder of the spiritual gift of faith. It conveys the idea of gazing at or focusing on God, and the joy and rejoicing that comes from a deep connection with Him. Living a life that is full of good works and acts of mercy, like Tabitha, is a reflection of a heart that is rooted in faith and obedience to God's will. It is a reminder to keep our eyes fixed on Him and to seek His kingdom and righteousness above all else.

historical_references.context: Tabitha, also known as Dorcas, was a disciple and a dear friend of the apostle Peter. She was known for her good works and acts of charity, particularly in making and mending garments for the poor. When she died, the believers in Joppa mourned for her deeply. Peter came to Joppa and raised her from the dead.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Eusebius, Church History 2.23.36-37 The name Tabitha carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Tabitha, the wife of Theophilus, was a wealthy and generous woman in Caesarea. She collected and distributed funds for the needs of the poor and the building of churches. She died, and her husband, Theophilus, donated her wealth to the church for charitable purposes, which became the 'Tabitha Fund'.

It also symbolizes a gentle and compassionate spirit, as Tabitha was known for her deeds of kindness and generosity.
